rule.title: block.timestamp, blockhash, or prevrandao used to gate value-transferring effect

intent.attack_thesis: TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH, or PREVRANDAO flows into a modulo or comparison operation that gates a value-transferring effect. These values are either miner-influenceable (TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH) or predictable before transaction execution, enabling exploitation of randomness-dependent state transitions.

reporting.title_template: Miner-influenceable block property gates value transfer
reporting.summary: Matches functions where TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH, or PREVRANDAO flows through MOD/AND/EQ into a condition that controls a value-transferring effect.
reporting.user_summary: This contract uses block properties (timestamp, block hash, or difficulty) as a source of randomness to decide who receives funds or a prize. Miners and validators can influence these values within a small window. An attacker acting as or colluding with a miner can time their transactions to win consistently.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies dataflow from TIMESTAMP/BLOCKHASH/PREVRANDAO/DIFFICULTY opcodes through arithmetic comparison (MOD, AND, EQ, LT, GT) into a branch guarding an asset_transfer or mint effect. No commit-reveal scheme, Chainlink VRF, or equivalent cryptographic randomness source is present.
reporting.exploit_narrative: An attacker (or miner/validator) computes which block timestamp or block hash produces a winning outcome. The attacker times their transaction to land in a block where the computation yields the favorable result, consistently winning lotteries, games, or randomized distributions.
exploit_preconditions: block property used in modulo or comparison gating value transfer
no cryptographically secure randomness source (VRF, commit-reveal)
remediation_hints: use Chainlink VRF or equivalent decentralized randomness oracle
implement a commit-reveal scheme where randomness is contributed before it can be predicted
avoid using block.timestamp or blockhash for randomness in any value-sensitive context

preconditions: randomness derived from block.timestamp or blockhash
attacker can predict or influence block property

steps.action: compute block timestamp/hash combination that produces winning modulo result; submit transaction in target block
steps.expected_state: randomness check evaluates favorably; asset_transfer or mint effect reaches attacker

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker receives prize/reward/tokens by exploiting predictable randomness source
environment_requirements: attacker with block timing control or colluding validator
